_doc: Security corpus: one file per case, as in v1. Each bug case carries one seeded vulnerability that security-review-edho-ferdian's checklist names; `keywords` must appear in a finding's summary or category for it to count, so a vague 'improve validation' near the line is not a catch. `bug: null` marks a clean control that does the risky thing safely.

01-link_preview.py.bug: Any http(s) URL from a chat message is fetched server-side, including internal addresses and cloud metadata endpoints.

02-session_cache.py.bug: pickle.loads runs on a value the client controls (a cookie), which is remote code execution.

03-profile-update.js.bug: Object.assign copies every request field onto the user, so a caller can set role, isAdmin, email verification or id.

04-login-redirect.ts.bug: `next` is redirected to unchecked, so a login link can send the user to an attacker's site.

05-webhook_auth.py.bug: The HMAC is compared with ==, which leaks timing; use hmac.compare_digest.

06-thumbnail_job.py.bug: The filename is interpolated into a shell=True command; a quote in the name breaks out of the quoting.

07-merge-settings.js.bug: deepMerge walks __proto__ from parsed JSON, so saved settings can pollute Object.prototype.

08-api_keys.py.bug: Passwords are hashed with salted SHA-1, a fast hash; use bcrypt, scrypt or argon2.
